:\u002201a09bc9-ec4d-77fb-92a3-768ffe844438\u0022,\u0022OwnerId\u0022:\u002201a04de3-7802-735b-872f-b95015c7216f\u0022,\u0022Text\u0022:\u0022StackedParentWatch: a child whose parent GitHub already merged and retargeted, but whose merge this platform has not recorded yet, reads as ParentMoved when the child does not contain the parent\\u0027s head (a parent that advanced after the child was cut). The replay that dispatches lands the child\\u0027s commits onto the merged parent\\u0027s own pull-request head while GitHub has already aimed the child at the base branch, so the parent\\u0027s already-merged commits replay instead of being dropped; the next sweep corrects it once the merge is recorded, but the lap is wasted and the pull request reads wrong in between. Candidate fix: when the parent\\u0027s head came from the refs/pull/N/head fallback because origin no longer has the branch, and this platform\\u0027s records do not yet say the pull request merged, report Unobservable rather than ParentMoved and let the next sweep answer. Weigh that against a child whose parent branch was deleted without ever merging, which would then sit quietly unobservable until ParentDead answers it.
